findings.title: earnings-stability value=maxDecline=0 yields 0.99 score when it fails on positive-years
findings.description: earnings-stability.js exports thresholdOp:'lte', threshold:0.50, value:maxDecline. A stock can fail (pass:false) because OpInc/FCF positive-year counts are below the needed floor while having maxDecline===0 (no positive-base year-over-year decline, e.g. consistently negative or flat OpInc). In score-aggregator.normalizeMethodScore the 'lte' branch executes `if (val <= 0) return 0.99;` BEFORE any pass/quality consideration of WHY it failed.
findings.mechanism: normalizeMethodScore: methodResult.pass is false so it does not return 1.0; op resolves to 'lte'; threshold=0.50 (non-zero); val=maxDecline=0; the lte guard `if (val <= 0) return 0.99;` fires and returns 0.99. earnings-stability carries weight 0.20 in SCORE_WEIGHTS.QUALITY_COMPOUNDER, so a QC candidate that fails earnings-stability purely on the positive-years requirement still receives ~0.99*0.20 of the composite from this method.
findings.reproducer: result={computable:true, pass:false, value:0, threshold:0.50, thresholdOp:'lte'} (loss-maker failing positive-year gate but with no >0-base decline). normalizeMethodScore(result,{thresholdOp:'lte'}) returns 0.99 instead of a low score. computeScore for QUALITY_COMPOUNDER then credits 0.99*0.20 toward the tier.
findings.impact: Loss-making or flat-OpInc stocks that fail the earnings-stability MUST get near-full credit (0.99) on a 20%-weight QC scoring input, inflating their QC score and potentially pushing genuine non-compounders into B/NEAR_MISS tiers. The distortion is invisible because the method correctly reports pass:false; only the score is wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: earnings-stability should not expose maxDecline (a magnitude where 0 means 'best') as `value` for graduated scoring while it can fail for an unrelated reason. Either (a) export a composite pass-distance as value, or (b) in normalizeMethodScore require val>0 before the 0.99 lte shortcut, falling through to the generic curve otherwise.

findings.title: fcf-yield uses sector MEDIAN as pass gate (no positive-only guard) — ~half of each sector passes
findings.description: fcf-yield.js calls H.effectiveThreshold(stock, 'fcf-yield', 0.05). effectiveThreshold returns the sector MEDIAN fcf-yield for the stock's sub-profile when available, replacing the 5% floor. Because it is the median, by construction ~50% of the sector clears the pass gate, and the threshold can be far below the intended 5% floor (verified live: HARDWARE _GLOBAL fcf-yield median = 0.0108 -> pass at >=1.1%; INDUSTRIAL 0.0398; HEALTHCARE 0.0270). Unlike roic/roce, 'fcf-yield' is NOT in POSITIVE_ONLY_METRICS in sector-medians-compute.js, so negative sector medians would be written verbatim and would set a negative (always-pass) threshold for loss-heavy sub-profiles.
findings.mechanism: sector-medians-compute._computeFromBuckets writes median(fcf/marketCap) for the 'fcf-yield' bucket including negative values (POSITIVE_ONLY_METRICS only covers roic,roce). effectiveThreshold step 2/3/4 returns that median as the threshold. fcf-yield.evaluate then passes when value >= median. Using a median as a binary pass threshold means the gate selects the top ~half of the peer group rather than enforcing the 5% economic floor.
findings.reproducer: node -e "const j=require('./methods/sector-medians-auto.json'); console.log(j.byRegion._GLOBAL.HARDWARE['fcf-yield'])" -> 0.0108. A HARDWARE stock with fcf-yield 1.2% (well under the 5% default) returns pass:true.
findings.impact: fcf-yield passes are not anchored to the intended 5% cash-yield floor; in low-yield sectors the gate degrades to 'beat half your peers', and any future sector with a negative median fcf-yield would pass essentially everything. fcf-yield carries weight 0.05 in QC SCORE_WEIGHTS and is a HG/QC prefer signal, so this leaks into scoring and the modes-report sort.
findings.suggested_fix: Decide intended semantics. If fcf-yield is an absolute floor, do not route it through effectiveThreshold (or clamp eff.threshold to >= the static 0.05 floor). If sector-relative is intended, add 'fcf-yield' to POSITIVE_ONLY_METRICS and use a percentile (e.g. p75) rather than the median for the pass gate, matching sector-relative-roic.

findings.title: fcf-yield sector median built from raw FCF but applied to SBC-adjusted yield (write/read mismatch)
findings.description: gatherBySubProfile pushes fcf/marketCap into the 'fcf-yield' bucket using annualFCF directly (raw, unadjusted). fcf-yield.js, however, computes fcfAdj = annualFCF - |annualSBC| and compares (fcfAdj/marketCap) against the bucket-derived threshold. The threshold is therefore calibrated on a systematically HIGHER (raw) yield distribution than the SBC-adjusted value it gates.
findings.mechanism: Write site (compute): fcf = _firstNonNull(annualFCF...); bucket pushes fcf/mc with no SBC subtraction. Read site (fcf-yield.evaluate): value = (fcf - |sbc|)/mc. For SBC-heavy sub-profiles (SAAS/HARDWARE) the adjusted value is materially below the raw-FCF median used as the threshold, so SBC-heavy stocks are penalized against a benchmark that did not pay the same SBC penalty.
findings.reproducer: A SAAS stock with raw FCF yield equal to the SAAS median (0.0476) but SBC = 3% of mcap evaluates to ~0.0176 adjusted and fails the 0.0476 median threshold, even though it is exactly median on the basis the threshold was built from.
findings.impact: Systematic, sector-dependent bias against SBC-heavy companies in fcf-yield pass/scoring; the median benchmark and the metric being gated are not the same quantity.
findings.suggested_fix: Make write and read sites consistent: either subtract |annualSBC| when building the 'fcf-yield' bucket in gatherBySubProfile, or compute the bucket and the method against the same (raw or adjusted) definition.

findings.title: _n_<metric> reports full array length while median/percentile use positive-filtered subset
findings.description: In _computeFromBuckets, for POSITIVE_ONLY_METRICS (roic, roce) the median and p25/p50/p75/p90 are computed from thresholdArr/useArr (values filtered to v > -0.05), but result[spId]['_n_'+mid] is set to arr.length (the FULL, unfiltered array). Consumers (lookupPercentile minN gate, modes-report n display, rolling-median n) read this inflated count as the effective sample size.
findings.mechanism: useArr may be much smaller than arr for distressed/loss-heavy sub-profiles. The minN>=5 guard (line 159 continue) ensures at least 5 positive values exist, but _n_ still advertises the full count, so a percentile computed from exactly 5 positive values can report n=200, overstating reliability.
findings.reproducer: A sub-profile with 200 roic entries of which only 6 are > -0.05: median is computed from 6 values, but _n_roic=200 is written and surfaced as the sample size.
findings.impact: Reliability gating and UI confidence (sectorN in sector-relative-roic, rolling n) overstate how many stocks backed the median/percentile. Mostly cosmetic but can let thin positive-only distributions look authoritative.
findings.suggested_fix: Report _n_<mid> as useArr.length (the array actually used), or add a separate _nUsed_<mid> field and have lookupPercentile/minN gate on it.

findings.title: roce sector medians/percentiles computed and written but never consumed by any method
findings.description: gatherBySubProfile builds and _computeFromBuckets writes 'roce' medians + p25/p50/p75/p90 into sector-medians-auto.json for every sub-profile and region, but no method consumes them: effectiveThreshold is only ever called with method ids 'roic' and 'fcf-yield', and there is no method whose id is 'roce'. lookupMedian/lookupPercentile are only invoked for 'roic'.
findings.mechanism: roce is a POSITIVE_ONLY_METRIC and is fully computed each pull (oi/(ta-cash) pushes, percentile enrichment) but is dead output — it inflates the medians file and adds compute with no downstream reader.
findings.reproducer: grep effectiveThreshold( and lookupMedian/lookupPercentile call sites across methods/: only 'roic' and 'fcf-yield' appear; 'roce' appears only in compute + lookup helper, never as a method id or a lookup metricName.
findings.impact: Wasted computation and file bloat each medians regeneration; no correctness impact. Flagged because it indicates a never-wired feature that may mask an intended roce-based method that was never added.
findings.suggested_fix: Either wire a roce-based sector-relative method (mirroring sector-relative-roic) or drop roce from the gather/compute path until needed.

findings.title: sector-relative-roic degraded mode ranks 90 (not 75) for roic in [p50, 1.5*p50)
findings.description: When p75 is absent the method enters degraded mode and sets p75 = p50 (line 160-166). _rankRoic evaluates, in order, roic>=p75*1.5(==p50*1.5)->100, roic>=p75(==p50)->90, roic>=p50->75. For any roic in [p50, p50*1.5) the function returns 90, because the roic>=p75 test fires before the roic>=p50 test once p75 collapses onto p50. The degraded cap (rank>90->90) does not lower it.
findings.mechanism: With p75 synthesized equal to p50, the intended 'at/above median = 75' band is shadowed by the 'at/above p75 = 90' band for the whole [p50, 1.5*p50) range, because p75 and p50 are the same boundary and the 90-bucket is tested first.
findings.reproducer: _rankRoic(0.12, 0.10, 0.10) (degraded p75=p50=0.10) returns 90; with a real p75=0.18 the same roic=0.12 returns 75.
findings.impact: In degraded mode (medians file pre-dates p75 keys, or first pull after a sector drops below minN), every stock merely at/above sector median is reported as rank 90 (strong top-decile signal) rather than 75. The pass gate (>=75) is unaffected, but the surfaced percentile and consumers reading components.sectorRank overstate the signal.
findings.suggested_fix: In degraded mode, cap rank at 75 for roic>=p50, or skip the p75 buckets entirely when degraded so the median bucket (75) is the ceiling.
